claims.statement: Taiwan's geopolitical risk index reached a historic peak in March 2026, with 0.3339% of newspaper articles covering Taiwan-related geopolitical tensions.

Taiwan's geopolitical risk spiked dramatically in May 2026 to 0.5347% of articles, representing the highest level in the entire 10-year data series and more than double the typical 2021-2025 baseline.
The historical Taiwan GPR index (gprhc_twn) reached 0.5016% in May 2026, the highest level since the series began in 1900, indicating unprecedented media attention to Taiwan geopolitical risk.
Taiwan's geopolitical risk remained elevated in October 2026 at 0.0821% of articles, though substantially lower than the May 2026 peak, suggesting some moderation in tensions.
The global GPR index reached 330.1768 in March 2026, more than triple the 1985-2019 baseline of 100, coinciding with Taiwan's elevated risk profile.
Taiwan's geopolitical risk showed a sustained elevation from March through June 2026, with gprc_twn averaging above 0.25%, significantly higher than the 2023-2025 average of approximately 0.20%.
Taiwan's geopolitical risk in August 2022 reached 0.7402% of articles, the previous historical peak before 2026, indicating that 2026 levels approached but did not exceed the August 2022 crisis.
Taiwan's geopolitical risk showed a declining trend from the May 2026 peak of 0.5347% to 0.0821% by October 2026, representing an 85% reduction over five months.

summary: Taiwan experienced a severe geopolitical risk crisis in early-to-mid 2026, with newspaper coverage reaching historic levels. The country's GPR index spiked to an unprecedented 0.5347% of articles in May 2026, the highest level in the entire modern data series [geopolitical:TWN:002]. This May 2026 peak also registered as the highest in the historical series dating back to 1900, at 0.5016% [geopolitical:TWN:003]. The crisis began with a dramatic escalation in March 2026, when Taiwan's risk index reached 0.3339% coinciding with a global GPR index of 330.1768, more than triple the historical baseline [geopolitical:TWN:001][geopolitical:TWN:005]. Risk remained elevated through June 2026, with sustained coverage above 0.25% [geopolitical:TWN:006]. However, by October 2026, Taiwan's geopolitical risk had declined substantially to 0.0821%, representing an 85% reduction from the May peak and suggesting significant de-escalation [geopolitical:TWN:004][geopolitical:TWN:008]. While the 2026 crisis was severe, it remained below the August 2022 peak of 0.7402%, which represents the highest recorded Taiwan geopolitical risk event in the data [geopolitical:TWN:007].
